E-challan Details:
DL127914240420121252 of vehicle bearing registration no. DL6SBC3514, dated 20.04.2024, issued against accused Sanjeev Kumar Roy, under section 39 r/w section 192 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "M.V. Act" in this judgment).

Brief Facts:

It has been alleged by the Prosecution that on 20.04.2024 at about 12:09 pm, at Khajuri Chowk,
Delhi falling within the jurisdiction of Khajuri Traffic Circle, motorcycle of the accused was found with a defective front plate and was also found to be using pressure horn and therefore was challaned for committing the offence under Section 39 r/w section 192 of M.V. Act, 1988.

3. It is pertinent to mention here that the cognizance of the offence had already been taken by Virtual Traffic Court and a fine was proposed for the summary disposal of the case under Section 208, M.V. Act.

The accused exercised the option to contest the present challan on the web portal of Virtual Traffic Court, pursuant to which the present challan was transferred to this Court for adjudication as per law.

Proceedings before the Court:
4. Accused Sanjeev Kumar Roy, entered his first appearance before this Court on 29.07.2024.
Notice under Section 274 BNSS was framed against him on 09.10.2025 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
The accused pleaded that he lives in PRANJALI PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH Date: 2025.12.19 TC No. 1156/2024 State vs. Sanjeev Kumar Roy 15:52:36 -0300 Palam and he never went to Khajuri Chowk.

sentences.text: The phone number mentioned on the challan does not belong to him.
He further pleaded that he contacted the concerned traffic officials, who called on the number on the challan and it was found that the number belongs to someone residing in Ghaziabad, U.P.

It was thus pleaded by him that he has not committed any offence in violation of the provisions of the M.V.
Act and the present challan has been wrongly issued against him by the Traffic Police.
5.
In order to prove its case, the Prosecution wished to examine two witnesses PW-1 ASI Brijpal and PW-2 HC Sunil.

PW-1 in his examination-in-chief brought on record the original challan exhibited PW1/A and deposed that on 20.04.2024, he was posted at Khajuri Traffic Circle at Khajuri Chowk as a ASI and on that day, at around 12:09 pm, a person was seen driving the motorcycle bearing number DL-6SBC-3514 without wearing helmet and using pressure horn.

He further deposed that he challaned the said motorcycle and took the signatures of the driver on the said challan at point B and also took the photographs but the same cannot be produced as the same are destroyed by the authority concerned within six months.
6.
In his cross-examination, PW1, deposed that on that day, accused Sanjeev Kumar Roy was not present at the spot and he was not driving the said motorcycle.
He further deposed that he could not produce the notification regarding the destruction of photographs of authority concerned.
PRANJALI PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH Date: 2025.12.19 15:52:44 -0300 7.

PW-2 in his examination-in-chief corroborated the testimony of PW1.
8.

After completion of Prosecution Evidence, the statement of accused was recorded on 01.12.2025 under section 351 BNSS wherein the entire incriminating evidence appearing against the accused State vs Sanjeev Kumar Roy on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141721249/
2 was put to him to which he stated that his vehicle has been wrongly challaned.
9. Thereafter, the matter was listed for Defence Evidence.

Accused examined himself as DW-1 and in his examination-in- chief, it was deposed by him that he has a pulser bike bearing number DL6SBC3514 and his bike does not have a pressure horn neither does it have a defective front plate.

He has placed on record the photographs of his bike as Ex. DW1/1.
Appreciation of Evidence:
10. I have heard the arguments advanced by the Ld. Addl. PP for the State as well as the accused and have carefully perused the entire record and evidence placed before the Court.
11.

In the present case, a violation of section 39 of M.V. Act has been alleged which reads as:-
Necessity of Registration:-
"No person shall drive any motor vehicle and no owner of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit the vehicle to be driven in any public place or in any other place unless the vehicle is registered in accordance with this Chapter and the certificate of PRANJALI by PRANJALI PRAKASH TC No. 1156/2024 State vs. Sanjeev Kumar Roy PRAKASH

sentences.text: Date: 2025.12.19 15:52:52 -0300 registration of the vehicle has not been suspended or cancelled and the vehicle carries a registration mark displayed in the prescribed manner: PROVIDED that nothing in this section shall apply to motor vehicle in possession of a dealer subject to such conditions as may be prescribed by the Central Government".
12. In the present case, a violation of section 192 of M.V. Act has been alleged which reads as:-

Using vehicles without registration:-
"(1) Whoever drives a motor vehicle or cause or allows a motor vehicle to be used contravention of the provisions of section 39 shall be punishable for the first offence with a fine which may extend to five thousand rupees but shall not be less than two thousand rupees for a second or subsequent offence with imprisonment which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees but shall not be less than five thousand rupees or with both:
PROVIDED that the court may, for reasons to be recorded, impose a lesser punishment.

(2) Nothing in this section shall apply to the use of a motor vehicle in an emergency for the conveyance of persons suffering from sickness or injuries or for the transport of food or materials to relieve distress or of medical supplies for a like purpose:

13. The cardinal principle of law in criminal cases is that the burden of proof lies upon the Prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Thus, in order to prove the guilt of the accused and to warrant his conviction, the Prosecution is required to establish beyond reasonable doubt that the accused had indeed committed the violations.
14. Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act casts a prohibition on the driving of any vehicle by a person unless the same is registered.
Using a pressure horn under Motor Vehicles Act is a serious offence attracting heftyfines and potential imprisonment as it causes noise/air pollution and causes safety risks.
The penalties for the violation includes fines upto Rs. 10,000/- to Rs. 12,000/-, impounding of the vehicle and possible license suspension for repeated offences.
The objective behind penalising use of pressure horn is that creates a safety hazard and may lead to sudden startling noise and increase accident risks.

15. In the present case, prosecution has placed on record the original challan wherein the same has been shown to bear the PRANJALI PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH Date: 2025.12.19 TC No.
1156/2024 State vs. Sanjeev Kumar Roy 15:53:08 -0300 name, contact number and address of the driver Ritik Kumar.

sentences.text: However, that the challan in question has been issued against the accused Sanjeev Kumar Roy for using his motorcycle with a pressure horn and defective front plate committing RC Violation.

It is pertinent to mention here that the accused has pleaded that the offending vehicle does not belong to him and his vehicle does not have a pressure horn and the prosecution has not brought on record any proof or documentary evidence to establish that the offending vehicle is the same as that of the vehicle of the accused.
Further, no photographs have been placed by the prosecution witness to corroborate their testimonies.
The photographs placed on record by the accused of his vehicle clearly shows that his vehicle does not have a defective front plate neither does it have a pressure horn.

16. Considering the evidence on record, this court is of the opinion that the prosection has not been able to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt and the accused has been successful in raising a doubt in the story of the prosecution.

Conclusion:
State vs Sanjeev Kumar Roy on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141721249/
4 17.

In view of the reasons stated above, this Court is of the opinion that with respect to the offence under Section 192, M.V. Act, 1988, the ingredients of the alleged offence of RC violation do not stand satisfied before this Court and the guilt of the accused has not been established beyond reasonable doubt.
PRANJALI by PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH
In light of the discussion above, accused Sanjeev Kumar Roy, S/o Ram Kripal Roy in the present case stands acquitted for the offences under Section 192 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
